claims.claim: Empty plastic water drum for water
claims.evidence: No photo shows the interior; cap is closed in both shots so emptiness and prior contents cannot be confirmed.

claims.claim: Drum is for water (implying food-grade/safe for water storage)
claims.evidence: Embossed '210' and '10.2KG' are generic drum codes, not a food-grade or water-safe certification mark; drum is pictured among mixed-color used industrial barrels on bare dirt, which is consistent with reclaimed chemical drums rather than dedicated water containers.

risks.risk: Prior contents may have been chemical/industrial rather than water, leaving residue or odor
risks.proof: Video or photo of the open interior and a close-up of any manufacturer/content label or UN hazard code on the base or shoulder
risks.if_unproven: priced as a used reclaimed drum of unknown prior contents, not as a dedicated food/water-grade container

risks.risk: Actual liter capacity unconfirmed (only a weight figure and a code are visible)
risks.proof: Photo of a capacity/liter marking or a measured fill test
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest plausible capacity for this drum size/type

risks.risk: Cracks, dents, or leaks on unseen sides or base
risks.proof: Photos of all sides, base, and a water-fill/leak test clip
Close-up photo of cap threads and gasket, plus a tip-test clip showing no leakage

risks.risk: Overall age and wear not assessable
risks.proof: Photo of manufacture date stamp if present

proof_requests: Open-lid photo/video of the drum's interior
Close-up of any content/hazard/UN code label on the body or base
Photos of all sides and the base for cracks or dents
Short clip of a fill/leak test
Close-up of cap and gasket condition
response.reason: The witness clearly identifies a used plastic drum with screw cap, so it can be priced at worst case as an unverified, possibly non-food-grade reclaimed barrel until interior and label proof are provided.
